title: Nutrition for Women Who Lift – NZ Guide
meta_desc: Discover evidence‑based nutrition for New Zealand women who lift: protein targets, iron tips, hormone‑cycle eating, affordable local foods and a weekly action plan.
intro: Strength training changes a woman's nutritional needs. This guide breaks down the extra protein, iron and hormone‑cycle considerations for NZ lifters and gives you practical steps you can start this week.

sections.heading: Protein Power for Body Recomposition
sections.body: Women who lift need more protein than the general population to support muscle repair and growth while losing fat. Research suggests 1.6–2.2 g of protein per kilogram of body weight per day for active women. For a 65 kg lifter that’s 104–143 g daily, spread over 3–4 meals to maximise muscle protein synthesis. Aim for 20–30 g of high‑quality protein each feed, and include a source within 30 minutes post‑workout for optimal recovery.
list: Calculate your target: weight (kg) × 1.8 ≈ daily grams
Split protein across 3‑4 meals + post‑gym shake
Prioritise complete proteins (animal or complementary plant combos)

sections.heading: Iron – The Hidden Deficiency in Active NZ Women
sections.body: Iron loss is common for women who train, especially with heavy sweating and occasional menstrual blood. NZ data shows 1 in 4 women of reproductive age have low ferritin levels. Aim for 18 mg of iron daily (27 mg if menstruating heavily). Pair iron‑rich foods with vitamin C to boost absorption and avoid calcium or tea/coffee at the same meal, which can inhibit uptake.
list: Red meat (beef mince, lamb) – 2.6 mg iron per 100 g
Kangaroo steak – 3.2 mg per 100 g (often cheaper than beef)

sections.heading: Eating with Your Hormone Cycle
sections.body: Hormone fluctuations affect appetite, glycogen storage and recovery. In the follicular phase (days 1‑14) estrogen rises, supporting protein synthesis – a good time to focus on strength sessions and higher protein intake. In the luteal phase (days 15‑28) progesterone can raise body temperature and carbohydrate cravings; include complex carbs and slightly more calories to maintain performance and mood.
list: Follicular (1‑14): Prioritise protein‑rich meals, lean meats, beans
Luteal (15‑28): Add whole‑grain carbs (sweet potato, oats) and healthy fats (avocado, nuts)
Track cycle in a simple app to adjust macros each phase

sections.heading: Affordable NZ Protein Sources & Supplements
sections.body: You don’t need pricey imported whey to hit your targets. Local options provide excellent value and support NZ producers. Consider these when budgeting:
list: Plain Greek yoghurt (NZ Brand: Meadow Fresh) – ~$4 per 500 g, 10 g protein per 100 g
Canned tuna in springwater – $1.80 per 95 g can, 23 g protein
Eggs (free‑range) – $5 per dozen, 13 g protein per 100 g
Kiwifruit protein powder (NZ‑made) – ~$30 per 500 g, 80 g protein per 100 g
